phase: ## Phase 2: MP3 copies in the wrapper
summary: Pass, with four new Nits (F5 to F8) and no Blocker or Major. Commit dcfad290 closes my Nits F1 and F2, the new lookup tests close F3, and the log fix closes F4. Both child processes still start without a shell, and no new file deletion risk appeared. The 118 checks of the r2 probe and the 98 committed tests passed. A2 is not applicable, and A6 shows no overstatement. HEAD is one commit after the audited commit, and that commit changes only the plan of another track.
nonblocking_findings: F5 [Nit] review-b: The claim that the working directory is never searched is too broad (scripts/sound-set.mjs:75, plan.md:163, green-p2.log:128-129). The code skips an empty PATH entry, but it still honors an explicit relative PATH entry. Rationale: with `PATH=.` the wrapper ran a fake `./ffmpeg`, and `bash` resolved `command -v ffmpeg` to the same file (probe INFO P4.relativeEntry.dot). The caller sets PATH and FFMPEG_BIN, so no trust boundary changes. Disposition: note; reword the comment, or skip each PATH entry that `isAbsolute` rejects. Candidate fix M19 keeps 98 of 98 tests green, and the relative-entry probes then report `ffmpeg not found`.

F6 [Nit] review-b: The earshot guard still accepts a folder and an empty value, because scripts/sound-set.mjs:67-72 checks EARSHOT_BIN with `accessSync` and X_OK only. Rationale: with `EARSHOT_BIN=''` and with a folder, the wrapper removed the old `alpha.ogg` and `alpha.mp3` (probe INFO P4.earshot.empty and P4.earshot.directory). The run then ended with `sound-set: earshot failed for alpha (tap/soft) with exit null`. Before this phase only the `.ogg` file was at risk, and `git checkout` restores the tracked files. Disposition: note or fix; apply the regular-file rule of `isExecutableFile` to the earshot path before any preparation. Candidate fix M18 keeps 98 of 98 tests green, and both probes then print `earshot not found` and keep both old files.

F7 [Nit] review-b: No committed test pins two rules of the new lookup. The first rule skips an empty PATH entry (scripts/sound-set.mjs:90), and the second rule rejects a file without the execute bit (:81). Rationale: mutant M2 (no skip) and mutant M4 (no `accessSync`) each keep 98 of 98 tests green, and the r2 probe fails on both. M2 restores the hazard that F1 closed (a planted `./ffmpeg` runs), and M4 restores the late failure `exit null` for a non-executable file. Disposition: note; add one case with an empty PATH entry and a planted `./ffmpeg`, and one case with a non-executable FFMPEG_BIN. Each case expects exit 1, the exact `ffmpeg not found` line, and zero earshot calls.

F8 [Nit] review-b: green-p2.log:114 records the pre-fix run as `1 failed, 93 passed (98)` and then names five failures. The numbers do not add up to 98. Rationale: mutant M21 (the wrapper of 6804d082) gave `1 failed | 3 passed (4)` for files and `5 failed | 93 passed (98)` for tests. red-p2.log:92 records `5 failed, 93 passed (98)`, so the `1` counts the failed file. Disposition: note; the orchestrator corrects green-p2.log:114 to `5 failed, 93 passed (98)`. No code is affected.
evidence: Provenance: `git rev-parse HEAD` printed 18cc25dfa5df0448208dd0926b6e90acbe3ef39b at the start, in the middle, and at the end of the audit, and this value is role_base_sha. The brief names audited commit a1b67c77ad77650bab5fafea8304abeb1b141d60, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor a1b67c77 HEAD` exited 0. Only commit 18cc25df follows it, and it changes only measure/tracks/asset_chibi_sprouts_r1_20261022/plan.md, a plan of another track. `git diff --quiet a1b67c77 HEAD -- scripts tests sounds measure/tracks/audio_game_integration_20261014 measure/runs/audio_game_integration_20261014 measure/tracks.md measure/generated` exited 0, so each audited path is equal at both commits. The working tree also equals a1b67c77 for those paths (exit 0). The phase_base_sha 16b398b595354f5da275268f1b32c8e864b9312a resolves to a commit.

Applicability: `git diff --name-status 6804d082..a1b67c77` lists seven paths. Two are code: scripts/sound-set.mjs (M) starts two programs and removes files, and tests/sound-set-lookup.test.ts (A) runs the wrapper. The other five are records: plan.md, green-p2.log, red-p2.log, measure/generated/status.md, and the plan of another track. The test strategy marks Phase 2 as `Applicable, reduced: argv, no shell`, so the role stays applicable. `git show --stat` shows that dcfad290 changes only scripts/sound-set.mjs (34 insertions, 26 deletions) and that bb9a1fd7 adds only tests/sound-set-lookup.test.ts (265 lines). The AC2 failure lines and the AC2 argv are unchanged, as green-p2.log:138 states and probes P1 and P2 confirm.

F1 closed: scripts/sound-set.mjs:74-97 accepts only a regular executable file (`statSync().isFile()` and `accessSync` with X_OK). It reads an empty FFMPEG_BIN as unset and skips an empty PATH entry. Probe P4 ran 15 failing lookups. Cases: an absent path; a non-executable file; a folder; a link to a folder; a dangling link; a link loop; /dev/null; a blank value; a path of 5,000 characters; a trailing slash on a file; a FIFO (it ended in 25 ms); a bare name that PATH lacks; an unset PATH; the default name found only in the current folder; a bare name found only in the current folder. Each run exited 1 with the exact `ffmpeg not found` line, made zero earshot calls, and created no output folder. Seven lookups that must work also passed: an empty FFMPEG_BIN; a folder named ffmpeg ahead of the real binary; a non-executable file ahead of the real binary; bad PATH entries; a link to a file; a relative path with a slash; a basename on PATH.

F2 closed: scripts/sound-set.mjs:112-132 checks both targets with `lstatSync` before it removes either one. Probe P5 gave exit 1, the exact `cannot prepare output` line, zero earshot calls, and both files kept. The four cases are: an `.mp3` folder with a stale `.ogg`; an `.ogg` folder with a stale `.mp3`; two folders; a read-only output folder. When the second entry is blocked, the first entry stays complete, the stale files of the blocked entry stay, and the third entry never starts. A set folder that is a regular file stops with the exact line and keeps the file. Six links at the two targets (to a file, to a folder, dangling) were replaced, and every destination stayed intact.

F3 closed: tests/sound-set-lookup.test.ts adds `resolves the default ffmpeg from PATH` and `resolves a basename FFMPEG_BIN through PATH`. Mutant M20 (the PATH loop never runs) failed 4 tests: the empty value, the PATH folder, the default, and the basename case. The r1 mutant of the same kind kept 91 of 91 tests green.

F4 closed: red-p2.log lines 6, 7, 41, and 77 now hold 16b398b595354f5da275268f1b32c8e864b9312a. A machine check of every 40-hex string in plan.md, red-p2.log, and green-p2.log found 40 strings, and `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` succeeded for all 40.

Process start: scripts/sound-set.mjs calls `spawnSync` twice, at :134 for earshot and at :145 for ffmpeg. Each call passes a program path and an argv array and sets no `shell` option. The file imports no exec, eval, or vm API (probe P0). Probe P2 used FFMPEG_BIN and EARSHOT_BIN names with `;`, `$()`, backticks, quotes, `&`, `|`, `<`, and `>`. All 8 runs exited 0, created no marker file, and sent the AC2 argv to ffmpeg. A copy with `shell: true` on either spawn created all marker files, so the check can fail.

Names: probe P3 gave the wrapper 20 invalid entry names and 9 invalid set arguments. Each run ended with the exact `bad name` or `bad set name` line, zero earshot calls, and no new file. A copy with a loosened name check wrote `sounds/evil.ogg` and `sounds/evil.mp3` outside `sounds/fake`. Names such as `--help`, `-i`, and `-x` pass the check, but ffmpeg receives absolute paths, so no name becomes an option. A set named `sets` leaves sets.json and chibi.json unchanged. The wrapper prints a design with a control character unchanged, as before this phase.

Lookup edge cases: an empty PATH, a leading colon, a trailing colon, and a double colon never reach the current folder (probe P4.emptyPathEntry, five checks). A real binary later on PATH still runs after an empty entry. A relative PATH entry such as `.` or `bin` is honored, as a shell does (F5; probe INFO P4.relativeEntry). The earshot guard is unchanged, so an empty EARSHOT_BIN and a folder both pass it (F6). The run then removes both old files of the first entry and ends with `earshot failed ... with exit null`.

Error output: probe P6 ran seven failure scenarios with a canary value in the environment. Two more checks pin the exact `ffmpeg failed` and `ffmpeg wrote no file` lines. Cases: ffmpeg absent; exit 3; exit 0 with the canary on stdout and stderr; no file written; earshot exit 4; a folder as ffmpeg; a bare name not on PATH. No line held the canary or an environment value of 12 characters or more. The wrapper echoes only the FFMPEG_BIN value that the caller set, and it never prints ffmpeg output. It still prints earshot output after a successful render, as before this phase.

MP3 files, live render: probe P1 ran the wrapper with the default PATH lookup, the real ffmpeg 8.0.1-3ubuntu2, and a stand-in earshot. The stand-in earshot copies the committed Ogg. The run exited 0, wrote 14 files, and printed the 15 expected lines. The seven MP3 files have the same SHA-256 as the committed files. Probe P8 gave four bad Ogg inputs (4 bytes, empty, 50 percent, 90 percent), and each ended with `ffmpeg failed` and no MP3 file.

MP3 files, hygiene: probe P1b found 0 tag lines in each committed MP3 file (`ffprobe -show_format -show_streams`). It also found none of these markers: ID3, TAG, Xing, Info, Lavf, Lavc, /home, the user name, the host name, or an e-mail address. A frame walk reads each file as whole MPEG-1 Layer III frames of 288 bytes at 96 kbps and 48000 Hz. Probe P7 shows that the AC2 flags remove Ogg tags and the ID3 header. Two controls without the flags show that the default encode adds an ID3 tag with Lavf and that an explicit map carries the comments.

Targeted tests: the four Phase 2 test files through heavy-run.sh gave 4 files passed and 98 of 98 tests passed. After the run, `git status --short -- sounds scripts tests measure/tracks/audio_game_integration_20261014` printed nothing. The SHA-256 over sounds/ is 68f9a40e4e5f60898e21899b0edd5f8707c6be4bbb304b285ed71e7a5a2e8376, equal to the r1 value. The test file tests/sound-set-lookup.test.ts writes only into `mkdtempSync` folders under the OS temp directory and leaves no folder behind. The old folder `~/.cache/opencode/sound set adversarial Y9gOA4` from 11:12:59 remains, and no new folder appeared.

Mutation run, tests: the four committed test files ran in a temp tree against 22 variants of the wrapper, through heavy-run.sh. The unchanged copy (M0) gave 98 passed. Sixteen of the 18 regression variants fail at least one test. Failed tests per variant: M1 (bare name checked in the current folder) 1; M3 (folder accepted) 2; M5 (empty value not unset) 1; M6 (ffmpeg guard removed) 3; M7 (no pre-check of the targets) 1; M8 (`.mp3` target not prepared) 2; M9 (no post-check of the MP3 file) 1; M10 (`shell: true` on ffmpeg) 17; M11 (loosened name check) 15; M12 to M17 (one dropped ffmpeg flag each) 2 each; M20 (dead PATH loop) 4. Two variants survive with 98 passed: M2 (empty PATH entry) and M4 (execute-bit check), and they are F7. The wrapper of 6804d082 (M21) fails 5 tests, so the five Red gap tests failed first, and candidate fixes M18 and M19 keep 98 passed.

Mutation run, probe: the fixed r2 probe ran directly (`--probe-only`) against the same 22 variants, because the probe is light. The unchanged copy (M0) and candidate fix M18 gave 118 of 118. Candidate fix M19 gave 117 of 118, and the one failure is the static check P0.hardeningLinesPresent. The probe fails at least one behavioral check on each of the 19 other variants (M1 to M17, M20, and M21). Failed checks per variant: M1 7; M2 5; M3 3; M4 2; M5 1; M6 22; M7 2; M8 5; M9 1; M10 6; M11 27; M12 12; M13 21; M14 12; M15 21; M16 12; M17 12; M20 22; M21 13. The probe sees both variants that the tests miss: M2 fails the five P4.emptyPathEntry checks, and M4 fails P4.closed.nonExecutableFile and P4.ok.nonExecutableBeforeRealIsSkipped.

Probe fix: the first probe-on-variant run ended early on M7, M20, and M21, because a check read a file that the variant had removed. It printed `fail=0` for M7. I fixed the probe: a missing file now fails the check, a crash prints `FAIL CRASH`, and `P0.checkCount` fails when fewer than 118 checks run. I also added two checks for the ffmpeg failure lines, because M9 passed the first probe. The probe results in this file come from the fixed probe.

A2: not applicable. `git diff 6804d082..a1b67c77 --text -- scripts tests sounds | grep -n -i -E 'published|draft|consent|anonymi'` printed nothing, so no draft-to-published flip exists. A6: measure/tracks.md is unchanged in the range and makes no claim about this track. Its `vulnerability audit` line at :259 belongs to another track. plan.md uses `resolved` and `resolves` only for the PATH lookup. Secret scan: the added lines of the range (without MP3 files) printed nothing for these patterns: api key, secret, bearer, password, credential, authorization, token, private-key headers, e-mail addresses, and IPv4 addresses.

Helper files: review-b-a1b67c7-probe.mjs (118 checks) and review-b-a1b67c7-mutants.mjs (22 variants, modes `--tests-only` and `--probe-only`) are the evidence of this round. Both read the repository and write only to mkdtemp folders under /tmp, which they remove. The r1 files review-b-6804d08-probe.mjs and review-b-6804d08-mutants.mjs can go. The r1 probe still passes 79 of 79 on the new wrapper, and the r2 probe holds every r1 check (six under a new name). The r1 mutants file runs on the new wrapper, but 4 of its 8 variants no longer apply, because they anchor to the old source. Variant M21 of the r2 file replays the old wrapper, and the orchestrator removes the r1 pair, because the role shell denies rm.

Limits: I did not run the real earshot render, the project-wide gate, tsc, or measure/doctor.sh, because Green and Review A own those results. I checked process, path, and metadata safety, not audio quality. A file with `chattr +i` was not tested, because it needs root. Not tested, for a later track: the AC2 argv pins no input format and no protocol list. So ffmpeg would parse untrusted media if a downloaded take replaced a set file. Independence: I did not read the Review A result files, and no CONTEST item reached Review B in this round.
